0.original: Guthjon is still reeling from your miraculous find.

25.original: Deliver the chunk of leonine to Urianger.

48.original: I had hoped we would find leonine, but to find that particular specimen is nothing short of a miracle.

49.original: I wouldn't believe it had I not seen it for myself.

50.original: Before you set it in the Talos, would you take it to Magnus?

51.original: For three long years he's believed she died for nothing. He must know the truth─that her sacrifice was not in vain.

52.original: We'll take it straight to him. You have my word. Thank you, Guthjon, for all your help.

53.original: Right, then. Let's not keep everyone waiting.

55.original: I can only imagine the look on his face when he sees that.

57.original: If you've come to complain about the trolley, you'll find no sympathy from me. I told you before it won't run, and you wouldn't listen.

58.original: Oh, but it will. Now that we have this.

59.original: Your name is engraved on it, along with your son's. It was a gift from your wife, Magnus. From Agna.

62.original: Take it. Do with it what you will.

63.original: Are you certain? It would delay our plans, but─

64.original: I said take it. It was you who found it, you who needs it.

65.original: Looking at that stone, all I can see is...is...

67.original: I hope you'll be there when the Talos stirs to life.

68.original: I'm sure she'd want you to see it.

69.original: Would you do the honors of delivering this to Urianger?

70.original: Finally we can move on to Nabaath Areng. Assuming this works, of course.

71.original: Sorry I couldn't be of more help. By the sounds of it, you have a knack for handling strange requests.

72.original: On the bright side, Urianger taught me a lot about the Talos and their hearts. I think I can help if they need further repairs.

73.original: You what!? By the gods, I didn't think it possible.

74.original: You found leonine? Truly? Then what are we waiting for─let's get that trolley moving!

76.original: Thou art returned, and with leonine it would seem.

77.original: As promised, the Talos hath been made ready to receive its heart, thanks in no small part to Jeryk, Thaffe, and Minfilia.

78.original: At last we shall return time to the timeless, this sentinel of stone, that we may press on towards Nabaath Areng.

79.original: Very good. Now, let us begin.

80.original: I only want what's best for her. If only she could see that...

81.original: <sniff> I'm fine. Really. It's just been a long day.

82.original: I must confess you've impressed me. I did not expect the Talos to be in such fine condition.

83.original: You've done us a kindness far greater than anything we deserve. Thank you. Thank you so much.

84.original: Just thinking about the trolley running down the tracks, gears churning─gods, I can't stop smiling!

85.original: Mine apologies for the delay. Minfilia and I had a private matter to discuss.

86.original: Which bringeth me to the question─how didst thou find Thancred during your search?

87.original: He spoke of Minfilia? Of his own accord? I see...

88.original: 'Tis well that he did, and with such candor.

89.original: I attempted to broach the subject before. Mine intention was to ensure no words remained unspoken between them, lest tragedy intercede. A regret I myself know all too well. Alas, in the end he refused to heed my counsel.

90.original: A time will come when they must face the reality of their circumstances. But I have faith that all will be well in time...

91.original: Now, let us not tarry any longer. The Talos and Nabaath Areng await.
